mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies / Companies Registry of the parent entity's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route (for states party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention): issue a notarized copy if required, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the designated Competent Authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs or State Chancellery). Consular legalization route (for non-Apostille states): obtain certification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction. The Apostille and Consular routes are mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence/Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies / Corporate Affairs Authority of the parent entity's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route (for states party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention): issuance of an Apostille by the designated Competent Authority after any required legalization. Consular route (for non-Apostille states): verified by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. These two paths are parallel and exclusive; no sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for WFOE Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the parent entity (notarized by a local notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the notary's signature is covered by the Hague Apostille Convention: obtain an Apostille on the notarized resolution from the local Competent Authority. If the state is not an Apostille member: after notarization, the resolution must be authenticated by the state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. Do not combine the two methods in any sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity's corporate secretary or official registry where the Articles are filed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for documents originating from Apostille member states: the original/certified copy endorsed with an Apostille certificate by the state's competent authority. Consular legalization for non-member states: documents must pass through the ministry of foreign affairs of the source jurisdiction and then the PRC consular section. Determining the applicable route is binary; the two mechanisms cannot be layered.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Solvency and Good Standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: for banks located in a Hague Convention member country, the letter is notarized (if needed) and then apostilled by the competent national authority. For banks in non-Apostille states, the letter is certified by the national Ministry of Foreign Affairs and subsequently legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. The Apostille and Consular legalization paths are mutually exclusive and must not be performed in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any WFOE formation, counsel must run on the parent entity, all shareholders, directors, officers, and any UBOs exceeding 25% a three-layered screen: (1) domestic PRC screening against the SAMR/NECC blacklist and the PBOC's financial intelligence list; (2) United Nations Security Council consolidated list, including the China-specific listings and the UN 1373 terrorist finance sanctions; (3) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, and non-SDN lists, plus EU/UK equivalent programs, using a real-time screening tool with immediate adverse-media alerts. The AML officer must also assess any connections to offshore wind equipment leasing and marine construction companies subject to secondary sanctions (e.g., certain PRC-named companies), and obtain a negative-match written report with date/time stamps for audit trail, as well as civil and criminal sanctions compliance certifications.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Reservation and Declaration System (accessible online via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System at www.gsxt.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every WFOE registered Chinese name must follow the four-tier structure: [Administrative Division] + [Trade Name] + [Industry/Professional Characteristics] + [Legal Form]. The legal form for the WFOE is 'Limited Liability Company'. The trade name must be in Simplified Chinese characters; the foreign investor's name may appear only as a Chinese transliteration (phonetic) in the trade name. No Latin letters, Arabic numerals, punctuation, or traditional Chinese characters are allowed in the registered name. The name must be distinctive and not identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered enterprise in the same or similar industry, as checked by the SAMR automated name-clearance system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is communicated through the online portal within three working days. The applicant, through counsel, must file a formal administrative appeal via the same SAMR portal within 15 days of the rejection, attaching a legal memorandum demonstrating that the proposed name is neither identical nor misleadingly similar to existing names, and that any sensitive token is supported by a ministerial approval. If the registry upholds the rejection, the applicant may lodge a secondary appeal to the provincial SAMR or the national SAMR, which must be decided within 30 days. The final administrative review is available under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, followed by a court challenge before an intermediate people's court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not permissible for a WFOE in the ISIC 4290 sector (offshore wind turbine pilings). SAMR requires the registered address to be a self-owned or leased physical premise, verifiable by lease agreement and property title. Both the tax authority (State Taxation Administration) and the bank conducting PBOC-regulated KYC require the business premise to exist at the time of registration and to be actively occupied. The industry's revenue-logic (heavy marine construction, project financing wires, letters of credit) demands the company maintain a physical site office with staff, contracts, and equipment procurement records; a virtual office will trigger tax deregistration, bank account freezing, and an adverse finding on substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for a site inspection: (1) visible company nameplate and signage at the registered address; (2) employees on site with valid labor contracts and social insurance; (3) original lease agreement and recent rent/utility bills; (4) board minutes and project meeting records evidencing actual management activities; (5) accounting vouchers, invoices, and bank statements stored on the premises; (6) a compliance folder containing the company chop, certificates, and AML/CFT policies. The quantified risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the municipal tax bureau or the SAMR is 65% in the first fiscal year and 40% in subsequent years, reflecting the high cross-border fund flows and Project Financing Wires in this sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 10, 12, 20-27, 31-40, 46-55, 57-67, 178-180; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 6, 12, 28-31; Regulations on Registration of Market Entities (State Council Decree No. 734, 2022), Articles 2, 9, 11-17, 26-30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), exercised through the local Municipal/District Market Supervision Administration at the company's registered address
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company (外商投资公司设立登记申请书) together with the Company Articles of Association and the Certificate of Incorporation (Business License / 营业执照)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the PRC Company Law for a WFOE; however, the Articles of Association must state a registered capital and shareholders must actually pay their paid-in capital within five years of incorporation (or a shorter period mandated by the actual investment project) unless the sector imposes special requirements. For offshore wind engineering, the registered capital must be sufficient to meet the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development qualification standards and contract performance requirements. There is no statutory blocked escrow account, but all paid-in capital must be remitted to the company's designated capital contribution bank account and must be supported by a verified foreign exchange capital account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [WFOE LTD.], A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ORGANIZED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA.

WHEREAS, the company was incorporated and the Articles of Association registered with the State Administration for Market Regulation; and

WHEREAS, the shareholders have subscribed to the registered capital and the board of directors has been entrusted with the initial corporate governance and administration;

NOW, THEREFORE, the first board of directors meeting, acting unanimously, hereby resolves and directs:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARE CAPITAL. The board acknowledges that the registered capital of the company is [amount in RMB or USD], divided into [number] shares of common stock, subscribed and issued to the sole shareholder. The board authorizes the general manager to procure all capital contribution payments and to issue official receipts and contribution certificates in accordance with the Company Law. Capital contributions shall be paid in cash or in-kind within the legal timeframe, and the corresponding paid-in capital shall be remitted to the company's designated capital contribution bank account before such contributions are deemed finalized.

2. BANKING AUTHORITY AND SIGNING RIGHTS. The board approves the opening of corporate bank accounts, including a basic deposit account, a foreign exchange capital account, and a general deposit account, at such Chinese commercial banks as management shall select. The legal representative and the general manager, acting jointly for amounts exceeding USD 100,000, and individually for routine operational amounts, are empowered to execute all account applications, resolutions, wire transfer instructions, letter of credit applications, and related financing documents. The finance officer is directed to maintain and reconcile all bank records.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the company shall be at [full address], and the company adopts the said address as its legal seat for statutory service of notice, tax registration, and judicial communications. The legal representative is authorized to execute any lease, sublease, or occupancy agreement and to file the registered office address with the Market Supervision Administration.

4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. The board appoints [Name] as Chairman and Legal Representative of the company, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and General Manager, [Name] as First Supervisor with statutory audit and oversight powers, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. The legal representative shall have full authority to represent the company in dealings with all administrative, judicial, and financial institutions, and to sign any contract, resolution, or document required for the company's operations. The general manager shall exercise day-to-day management authority and shall cause this resolution to be implemented.

5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND SEAL MANAGEMENT. The board approves the creation of company, financial, and legal representative seals through a licensed seal engraving company registered with the Public Security Bureau. All seals shall be safeguarded by the finance officer and used only upon approval. The board orders the adoption of internal control standards, anti-money-laundering measures, and a compliance manual, and authorizes the general manager to submit the company's registration, tax, social insurance, and industry qualification applications.

This resolution is effective immediately and remains in full force until repealed or amended by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Pre-approval and Foreign Investment Information Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the unified National Enterprise Registration and Foreign Investment Information System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the national enterprise registration platform (sbj.samr.gov.cn) and create a real-name authenticated account with the proposed legal representative. Submit the proposed Chinese company name, the English trade name, the registered capital, business scope covering offshore wind turbine piling and marine engineering, and place of incorporation. The SAMR name-review system will preliminarily screen the name against prohibited words, similarity with existing enterprises, and protected intellectual property. After the name receives a preliminary clearance, complete and submit the Foreign Investment Information Report to MOFCOM through the same unified system, disclosing the ultimate beneficial owner, project nature, and estimated contributions. The system will issue a name pre-approval notification and a foreign investment filing receipt, both of which are needed for the formal incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Completed online name pre-registration application form
Passport or identification documents of the foreign investor and proposed directors
Power of attorney signed by the foreign investor appointing the local formation agent
Proposed Articles of Association in Chinese
Description of business scope and project details
Coordination letter or lease intention agreement for the proposed registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected due to conflict or prohibited terms, file a modified name application with fresh documentary evidence within five business days. If the foreign investment report is suspended by MOFCOM for incomplete beneficial ownership information, provide corrected declarations within ten days or obtain a temporary filing number and proceed with the incorporation application while curing the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Substantive Incorporation Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or District Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) in the city where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation dossier either electronically through the local government service portal or in person at the registration hall. The registration officer will verify the Articles of Association, the constitutive documents, the registered address lease, and the capital contribution schedule. The company must draft the Articles of Association in the prescribed form, including the corporate name, registered capital, shareholder obligations, scope of business, governance structure, and authorized representative provisions. After verification, SAMR will enter the company into the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and issue the Business License, a Certificate of Incorporation containing the unified social credit code. Following issuance, the company must complete statistical registration and tax registration, and must ensure that the foreign investor information has been successfully reported to MOFCOM.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company
Executive stockholders' resolution or sole shareholder decision
Notarized and legalized passport/ID of the foreign investor
Notarized Articles of Association signed by the investor
Lease agreement for the registered address and proof of property ownership
Appointment of legal representative and supervisor with signed acceptance
Foreign investment information filing receipt
Name pre-approval notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected for material omissions, correct the defects within seven working days and re-submit through the same online or physical window. If the rejection is based on an evaluative issue, submit a petition for administrative reconsideration to the superior Market Supervision Administration within fifteen days of receipt of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Seal Carving, Tax Registration, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) authorized seal engraving service; State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax bureau; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) social insurance agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after obtaining the Business License, apply to a Public Security Bureau-designated seal engraving enterprise for the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. The seals must be carved with the unified social credit code and registered in the PSB seal administration system. After the seals are obtained, register with the local tax bureau through the electronic tax service (e-Tax), obtain the tax payer registration number, select the VAT taxpayer type, and apply for invoice quota and general VAT payer status if monthly turnover is expected to exceed the threshold. Simultaneously register the company and future employees with the social insurance agency to create pension, medical insurance, unemployment, work-related injury, and maternity insurance accounts. Failure to complete tax and social insurance registration within the statutory grace period may result in late-filing penalties and fictitious entry in the credit system.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copies
Legal representative identification document
Seal registration application forms
Non-stamp-declaration letter or official stamp confirmation
Articles of Association and capital contribution schedule
Enterprise bank account information (basic deposit account)
Lease contract for the registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal carving registration is queried due to an unverified legal representative identity, present the legal representative to the PSB authorized service for biometric validation. If tax registration is overdue, submit an explanation letter and apply for a cutting off of the penalty through the tax bureau's administrative review process. Any social insurance non-registration notice must be handled by filing the full employee roster and paying the shortfall contributions with interest within the grace period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Exchange Registration and Foreign Investment Capital Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through designated banks, and the company's chosen commercial bank in China
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after issuance of the Business License, the legal representative or authorized agent must complete the Foreign-Invested Enterprise FDI Information Registration at a designated bank acting on behalf of SAFE. The bank will verify the foreign investor's identity, the business license, the Articles of Association, and the approved capital contribution schedule. Upon successful registration, the bank opens a foreign exchange capital account (capital account) for receiving the paid-in shareholder funds from abroad. The overseas shareholder must remit the registered capital in the name of the investing entity, using a proper remittance purpose code that matches the FDI registration. The bank will settle the foreign exchange against the registered capital into RMB only after checking the transaction background and anti-money laundering compliance. For project financing wires and letters of credit, the company must also open a general deposit account and prepare a facility operation and settlement arrangement for its offshore wind piling contracts.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copy
FDI registration form completed and signed
Foreign investor's identity certificate and passport
Articles of Association and capital contribution agreement
Certificate of Incorporation and unified social credit code
Proof of outward remittance instructions
Bank account opening forms and anti-money laundering questionnaire
Board resolution authorizing account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FDI registration is suspended because of a mismatch between the declared registered capital and the actual remittance amount, apply to the bank for a correction within ten working days, providing an amended capital contribution schedule or a shareholder resolution changing the registered capital amount. If SAFE later issues a penalty notice for delay, submit a mitigating explanation and evidence of compliance attempts to the local SAFE branch for administrative reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industry Qualification and Offshore Construction Licensing for Wind Turbine Piling Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD) Qualification Management Center and the local Maritime Safety Administration (MSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before engaging in offshore monopile foundation installation, submit an application to MOHURD for the Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate covering offshore works (port and waterway engineering general contracting or marine engineering specialized contracting). Prepare a detailed dossier evidencing the company's technical staff, registered construction engineers, welders, riggers, and pilotage standards, as well as the ownership or lease commitment of hydraulic hammers, vibratory hammers, jack-up vessels, and offshore cranes. After receiving the construction enterprise qualification, apply to the local Maritime Safety Administration for an Offshore Works Navigation Safety Assessment, which involves reviewing the installation plan, marine traffic impact, and emergency response plan. The local emergency management department will additionally issue a Safety Production License after site inspection verifies compliance with occupational health and offshore safety management systems. No physical monopile installation may begin until the navigation warning notice is published and the oil spill containment plan is approved.
required_dossiers: Construction enterprise qualification application form
Detailed engineering and construction method statement for offshore monopile driving
List and proof of owned or long-term leased heavy equipment
Registration documents for construction engineers and marine safety officers
Offshore safety management manual and emergency response plan
Work injury insurance policy and public liability insurance
Maritime Safety Administration navigational safety assessment application
Oil spill contingency plan and marine pollution response contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOHURD rejects the qualification because of insufficient technical personnel, hire and register qualified engineers, update the staffing table, and re-submit within thirty days. If the Maritime Safety Administration suspends the navigation safety assessment due to environmental or traffic concerns, revise the construction schedule, adopt additional safety measures such as off-peak pile driving windows, and resubmit to the MSA. Any delay in Safety Production License issuance may be cured by accelerating the workplace safety audit and correcting all flagged deficiencies against the Occupational Health and Safety Administration code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD) Qualification Management Center; Maritime Safety Administration (MSA) of the People's Republic of China; local Emergency Management Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate (Port and Waterway Engineering or Marine Engineering Specialized) and Safety Production License under the Regulations on Safety Management of Construction Works

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China, and the provincial Marine Ecology and Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Report (Category A) under Article 20 of the PRC Environmental Impact Assessment Law and Article 8 of the Marine Environment Protection Law. The project is classified as a marine construction work requiring an environmental impact report with marine ecological baseline surveys, public hearings, and prior approval by the competent forestry and marine authority before construction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Quantitative compliance thresholds: all treated effluent discharged from piling vessels and onshore supporting facilities must contain oil content ≤15 mg/L, suspended solids ≤100 mg/L, and no visible oil sheen. Drilling mud and cuttings must be discharged in approved offshore dump zones only and must contain oil content ≤15 mg/L, mercury ≤0.001 mg/L, and cadmium ≤0.01 mg/L. Underwater piling noise must not exceed a peak sound pressure level of 160 dB re 1 μPa at 750 m from the source; persistent underwater noise above 140 dB re 1 μPa must be mitigated using bubble curtains or alternative quieter driving methods. Hazardous hydraulic fluids and oily wastes must be stored on board in sealed containers and disposed at licensed hazardous waste facilities complying with GB 18597-2023 (Hazardous Waste Storage) and GB 18598-2019 (Hazardous Waste Landfill Controls). Stationary combustion engines used for piling power must meet the Stage VI emission limits for non-road mobile machinery under GB 17691-2018, particularly for nitrogen oxides at 0.4 g/kWh and particulate matter at 0.015 g/kWh. All waste discharges shall be recorded and reported to the Marine Environment Monitoring Center monthly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The onshore project office and steel pile assembly yard must obtain a civil defense construction inspection record and a fire safety acceptance certificate from the local fire and rescue authority, including proof of structural load inspection, installation of automatic fire alarm and suppression systems, and approved emergency evacuation routes. Offshore, all vessels and lifting equipment must hold current marine classification certificates issued by the China Classification Society, and dynamic positioning and navigation safety clearances from the Maritime Safety Administration. The company must obtain a workplace occupational health hazard evaluation certificate from the local health authority, covering noise, vibration, dust, and confined-space entry, and every crew member must hold an offshore survival, first aid, and marine firefighting certificate approved by the national maritime training authority. The fire permit is mandatory for any temporary living quarters and fuel storage on the installation vessels or artificial islands.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online administration is conducted through the National Tax Service Platform (e-Tax), the China International Trade Single Window for customs-trade data integration, and the VAT Invoice Management System under the Golden Tax Phase IV architecture.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a China-incorporated WFOE, the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) upon approval of the Articles of Association and incorporation is the sole statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT taxpayer ID. Tax registration is completed through the one-stop integrated registration mechanism at formation: SAMR automatically pushes the USCC and legal-person registration data to the competent STA office; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. If the automatic push fails, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration at the competent tax authority within 30 days of the SAMR business license issuance using the standardized registration application available in the e-Tax system, submitting the business license, approved articles of association, shareholder identity documents, legal representative identity materials, and proof of registered office. A foreign non-resident enterprise without an establishment in China but deriving Chinese-source income must register as a Non-Resident Enterprise with the competent tax authority at the location of the payer or real estate/property location in order to obtain a TIN; the application requires the foreign incorporation certificate, tax residence certificate, contract evidencing Chinese-source income, and the withholding agent engagement details. For the WFOE itself, the USCC is used for all VAT, Corporate Income Tax (CIT), individual withholding, stamp duty, and export VAT refund filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election for a WFOE limited-liability company. The WFOE is mandatorily classified as a Chinese resident enterprise subject to CIT on worldwide income, and as a general VAT taxpayer once annual taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; below that threshold it may elect simplified small-scale taxpayer treatment for VAT, but this is an invoicing and VAT-rate election, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover within a rolling 12-month period for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; the WFOE is nevertheless required to complete tax registration immediately upon corporate formation regardless of turnover. Small-scale taxpayers with monthly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 (quarterly RMB 300,000) are exempt from VAT on domestic sales, but exporters must generally register as general VAT taxpayers to claim zero-rating and input-VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue all VAT invoices through the National VAT Invoice Management System under the mandatory Full Digital Electronic Invoice (FDEI) regime. FDEI are digitally signed by the STA, carry the tax authority's unified electronic seal, and are transmitted in real time through approved APIs to the Golden Tax Phase IV platform. Paper invoices, if still permitted in transitional zones, must be synchronised with the VAT Invoice Management System before the end of the fiscal month, and no private offline invoicing is lawful. The system performs real-time cross-matching of Invoice, Tax control, Customs export declarations, and foreign exchange collection records; discrepancies automatically trigger tax-risk alerts and may suspend the VAT invoice allocation quota.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered general VAT taxpayer may apply 0% VAT and claim a refund of attributable input VAT on export sales of offshore wind turbine pilings only when the goods physically leave China, the export is declared to and released by China Customs, the title and risk have passed to the overseas buyer, the sales proceeds are received from a non-resident payer, and the export is not listed on any prohibited or suspended export goods catalogue. For offshore installation and marine construction services performed outside China for non-resident clients, the zero-rating or exemption eligibility additionally requires that the service is supplied from China but consumed entirely outside China, with a written contract stating offshore consumption and evidence of actual delivery outside China. The statutory documentation package must evidence the commercial reality of the cross-border transaction, not merely corporate form.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration filed through the China International Trade Single Window and stamped/released by China Customs, including the assigned export declaration number
Bill of Lading or sea waybill evidencing shipment of the pilings to the overseas buyer and the port of discharge
Commercial invoice and export sales contract specifying INCOTERMS and transfer of risk to the non-resident buyer
Packing list and export goods inspection certificate (CIQ) where the pilings fall within mandatory inspection catalogue

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued Export Proceeds Collection Confirmation evidencing that the foreign exchange from the overseas buyer was collected and repatriated into the WFOE's domestic foreign-exchange settlement account
Foreign Exchange Collection Verification record digitally submitted to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the settlement bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA uses Golden Tax Phase IV data matching with China Customs and SAFE to verify export declaration, physical outbound shipment, invoice consistency, and foreign-currency repatriation. Any false export declaration or fraudulent VAT refund claim triggers immediate clawback of the full refunded input VAT, a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid or clawed-back tax under the Tax Administration and Collection Law, and an administrative penalty of 50% up to five times the falsely refunded amount. Where the fraudulent amount is significant, the case is referred to the criminal authorities; Criminal Law Article 204 provides for fixed-term imprisonment or life imprisonment in the most aggravated cases, together with a fine of one to five times the fraudulent refund and confiscation of the taxpayer's VAT invoice issuance privileges, downgraded tax credit rating, and mandatory post-refund inspection status for a period of at least three years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a bank-led current account convertibility regime with registration-based capital account management. A WFOE may freely settle current account receipts and pay current account obligations through designated banks after documentary authenticity review, but capital account receipts, including equity and debt injections, must be matched to a SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration and a specific purpose code before entry. Currency conversion itself is not prohibited, but the funds are ring-fenced: FDI capital settled into RMB must be used within the WFOE's approved operating scope and is not freely available for portfolio investments, entrusted loans, real estate beyond negative-list limits, or unregulated domestic lending. Profit and dividend repatriation requires audited financial statements, tax compliance certification, and SAFE/bank current-account outflow declaration. For a cross-border wind-monopile installation WFOE, the operative constraint is not convertibility at the spot tier but the capacity to evidence commercial authenticity for every USD or CNY payment, especially marine charter hire and offshore service invoices. Full capital-account convertibility is absent; the constituent regime is current account free convertibility plus registered capital account managed convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory conversion ratio: none. The pre-2010 mandatory surrender policy was replaced by an autonomous foreign-currency retention regime. The WFOE must repatriate export and service proceeds through designated foreign exchange banks and may either retain the receipts in foreign currency or convert them into RMB. For goods export proceeds, collection should occur within the contractually agreed payment terms and is monitored by the bank under SAFE trade inventory rules; where open-account export proceeds remain unreceived beyond 180 days after customs declaration, the bank and exporter must report to SAFE and provide a commercial explanation. For offshore wind installation service revenue, proceeds should be received within the invoice maturity and supported by signed contracts, completion certificates, and tax filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account
FDI Capital Settlement Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account
FDI Capital Settlement Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMIs are not viable as primary treasury rails for a mainland WFOE because they lack a People's Bank of China payment license and cannot participate in SAFE's current and capital account purpose-code declaration architecture. They may support the offshore parent treasury, but the WFOE itself must maintain clearing, FX settlement, and compliance accountability at a licensed tier-1 domestic commercial bank. A local licensed third-party payment institution may provide ancillary cross-border RMB collection, but it cannot replace the corporate bank account for statutory FDI capital verification and project trade settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the first opening of the RMB basic deposit account and FDI capital settlement account, the WFOE legal representative or a formally appointed local officer holding an original notarized power of attorney must normally attend an in-branch KYC interview. Remote consular proxy-only opening is not a standard SAFE or bank-accepted route for full account activation. The bank will verify the company seal, registered address, controlling persons, and operating substance, and may require a video interview plus on-site inspection for high-value marine construction accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain with an offshore holding parent and multiple intermediate shell layers above the mainland WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation, current constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders for every entity in the ownership chain, audited financial statements, a full organizational chart with percentage holdings, UBO declarations with copies of national identity documents and passports, source-of-wealth statements for every person with 10 percent or more beneficial ownership, and any trust or nominee declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to shipowners, vessel charterers, and port-service payees located in flag-of-convenience or high-risk maritime jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO number, flag state registry certificate, ISM and ISPS certificates, Protection and Indemnity insurance certificate, charter party and sub-charter party contracts, detailed vessel invoices, AIS track records for installation activity, sanctions and enforcement screening reports confirming no match against OFAC, EU, UN and other restricted lists, and project-specific end-use statements for marine assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the licensed construction scope and actual payment nature, including large mobilization payments, rental of hydraulic hammers, or lease of installation vessels without clear project linkage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business license showing construction scope aligned with ISIC 4290 and NAICS 237990, statutory offshore construction permits, executed turnkey installation contract, detailed project schedule with mobilization and demobilization milestones, equipment and vessel lease agreements, invoices, progress valuations from the employer, and a treasury confirmation letter showing how each payment maps to a completed work stage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party remitter funding or round-tripping capital that does not match the declared shareholder identity and registered capital structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving capital injection, original SWIFT remittance instructions identifying the remitter as the registered shareholder, bank statements from the remitting entity showing the source of funds, intercompany loan or support agreement for any supplemental funding, shareholder register, SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Business Registration form, and a People's Republic of China certified public accountant capital verification report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent company must complete SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration for the WFOE, either delegated to a qualifying Chinese bank or filed directly with SAFE. The overseas parent then wires USD or cross-border RMB through SWIFT MT103 into the WFOE's designated FDI Capital Settlement Account, including the SAFE registration reference, the shareholder remitter identity, and the capital-account purpose code corresponding to equity investment in a foreign-funded enterprise. The receiving bank verifies the memorandum and articles of association, capital contribution resolution, shareholder register, banking license of the remitter, and remitter/beneficiary relationship. After arrival, the WFOE engages a registered PRC CPA to issue a capital verification report, and the bank releases the funds for permitted operating uses under the Foreign Investment Negative List after completing the SAFE capital item declaration. Any injection exceeding the registered amount requires an amended SAFE registration before funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should be segmented by instrument. Direct service and equipment payments are settled through SWIFT MT103 against a contract, invoice, performance certificate, and tax withholding certificate where applicable. Imported monopile steel, tower sections, grouting materials, and heavy lifting equipment can be settled under commercial letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700, with the WFOE as applicant and overseas fabricator as beneficiary. Documentary collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis are acceptable for established relationship-based trade. For charter-hire of installation vessels and offshore support vessels, the bank will require the IMO number, charter party, and operating expense invoices to clear the purpose code. Cross-border RMB clearing should run through CIPS, while USD flows use the CHIPS correspondent network; all payments remain subject to sanctions screening and transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD FX forward contracts supported by genuine current account or project-related exposure under SAFE real-need requirements
Cross-currency swaps limited to foreign currency debt service, FDI capital repatriation, or project finance obligations of the WFOE
Plain-vanilla FX options and bank-approved option combinations for tendering and project cash flow hedging

Onshore CNY non-deliverable forwards are not generally available for a mainland WFOE; offshore CNH NDF activity, if any, must be confined to the offshore parent treasury and cannot be used to create speculative RMB exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (annual report publication on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Administration for Market Regulation via NECIPS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - June 30 of each year covering the preceding calendar year; the WFOE must file before 30 June of the immediately following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory window results in inclusion on the 'List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations'; the record becomes publicly searchable and blocks banking, bidding, procurement, tax facilitation, and government incentive activities. The enterprise may cure by publishing a late annual report and applying for removal, but if the non-compliant status persists for three consecutive years, SAMR transfers the entity to the 'List of Enterprises with Serious Illegal and Dishonest Acts' and proceeds toward administrative disqualification, forced deregistration/revocation of the business license and individual responsibility sanctions for directors/legal representatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report (annual report of the foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) in conjunction with the State Administration for Market Regulation; filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System / Foreign Investment Integrated Management System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - June 30 of each year for the preceding calendar year; no extension is published for ordinary WFOEs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate filing creates an adverse credit and investment information record. After reminder/order by MOFCOM, a continuing refusal to report may trigger administrative penalties under the PRC Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures, adverse effects on future foreign exchange procedures, project financing, letters of credit and bank relationships; persistent violations can be escalated to credit-regulation enforcement and may affect the qualification, approval, licence and market-access standing of the offshore wind construction entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement (annual enterprise income tax return and tax reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local tax service bureau or online tax platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The final settlement and annual return must be filed within five months after the close of the taxable year, i.e. by May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues overdue tax surcharge at the rate of 0.05% per day until paid; late filing exposes the WFOE to fines of up to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases or RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases, plus possible denial of tax credit benefits and enforced collection measures by the tax authority; continuous deliberate non-filing may result in tax audit, freezing/attachment of bank accounts, restriction of export, exit restrictions on the legal representative and responsible financial officers, and in extreme cases referral for administrative/penal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual financial statement audit by a licensed PRC CPA firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed as a stand-alone government return; the audit opinion is addressed to the shareholders and board, and the audited financial statements form the evidentiary basis for the SAMR annual report, CIT final settlement, SAFE report and any MOHURD licence-supporting filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be completed before the shareholders' meeting considering the annual financial report and, in practice, before the April 30 - May 31 tax final settlement deadlines; the WFOE must deliver audited statements to all shareholders within the period prescribed by the articles of association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have annual financial statements audited violates the PRC Company Law and exposes the company, directors, supervisors and senior executives to regulatory orders, fines, shareholder disputes and evidentiary disallowance of financial statements. SAMR/SAFE/tax authorities may treat unaudited or non-verified statements as defective annual-report data; repeated breach undermines the filing status of the WFOE, can be recorded in credit-discipline files, and may disqualify licence qualification or annual credit assessment in the marine engineering market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Exchange Direct Investment Statistics Registration (FDI stock rights and interests registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through designated banks or the Foreign Exchange Integrated Management Information Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - June 30 of each year; the registration covers the direct investment stock, equity ratios, assets/liabilities and income as of the preceding year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or untruthful reporting is treated as a foreign exchange administration violation; SAFE or its delegated bank may axe foreign exchange payment/receipt/transfer convenience for the WFOE, clamp cross-border project financing wires and letters of credit, impose administrative penalties, and list the entity for targeted examination; prolonged non-compliance can suspend the company's SAFE records and impair dividend repatriation, capital injections and offshore guarantee registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: China does not apply size-based balance-sheet, turnover or headcount exemptions for corporate statutory audits. Under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company, including a WFOE, must submit its annual financial report to an accounting firm for audit at the end of each fiscal year. The WFOE is therefore legally audit-required from the first day of its operation irrespective of whether total assets exceed zero, revenue is nil, or headcount is zero. Additional triggers: possession of a marine/construction engineering qualification for ISIC 4290 offshore monopile driving requires audited financial capacity statements in licence applications/inspections; foreign parent consolidation or IFRS reporting may require a bridging audit; an enterprise entering mortgage, share pledge, letter-of-credit or project-financing arrangements will be contractually and regulatorily required to maintain certified audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance, including the Basic Standard, specific accounting standards, application guidance and interpretation bulletins; CAS are substantially converged with IFRS. Full CAS apply to most WFOEs; the simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises may be used only by entities that satisfy the state-defined small-enterprise criteria and not by any WFOE preparing statutory financial statements for cross-border consolidation, direct investment, credit or licencing purposes unless formally permitted. Books and statutory financial statements must be kept in RMB; IFRS-basis supplementary packs may be prepared for the foreign parent but cannot substitute for the statutory CAS audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain a compliant beneficial-ownership file. Any shareholder/equity transfer, capital increase/decrease, direct or indirect controlling-interest change, or change in ultimate beneficial owner (an individual holding 25% or more of the equity or otherwise having effective control through another layer) must be documented in the statutory register and filed through the SAMR alteration channel within 30 calendar days of the event. The annual enterprise credit information report serves as the annual confirmation of the registered equity/ownership profile, and the beneficial-owner information maintained in the SAMR/UBO database must be true and current as of June 30. The 30-day reporting window also applies to transfers of registered shares, pledge/changes of registered capital, legal representative changes, directors/supervisors/executives changes and registered-office changes; failure to update creates evidentiary/registration priority problems and administrative credit penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) showing all equity transfers, pledges and capital contributions
Register of Directors and, where applicable, Register of Supervisors
Register of Senior Management Officers (legal representative, general manager, CFO, chief accountant and equivalents)
Register of Charges/Mortgages/Security created over registered assets, shares or contract rights (including SAMR- and credit-registry-filed security records)
Minute Book containing resolutions of shareholders, board meetings, supervisor meetings and executive decision records
Statutory accounting ledgers, vouchers and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for a registered office and corporate secretarial/agent service in second-tier mainland cities; USD 1,200 - 3,000 per year in Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen or where continuous liaison with SAMR, tax, bank, SAFE and notarial channels is required
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 15,000 for a moderate-size WFOE with simple related-party lending and no active offshore-wind contracts; USD 20,000 - 60,000 for a project-performing ISIC 4290 entity with marine equipment assets, contract-work-in-progress, cross-border parent consolidation, IFRS bridging, foreign exchange registration and supporting certification for construction licences

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For an offshore wind piling WFOE, the general corporate income tax rate is 25%. Preferential regimes may include: (i) 15% reduced rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; (ii) 100% super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures; (iii) potential 3-year exemption and 3-year 50% reduction for qualifying public infrastructure projects under the Catalogue, if the monopile installation project is classified as public infrastructure; (iv) temporary preferential effective rate of 5% for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; (v) certain regional incentives (e.g., Hainan Free Trade Port 15% for encouraged industries). No general patent box regime exists in China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Type A), supplemented by core schedules (e.g., A101010, A104000, A105000, A106000), filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal of China.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 May of the following calendar year if the fiscal year ends on 31 December). Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from offshore wind monopile installation contracts (ISIC 4290 / NAICS 237990) recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record all contract revenue when performance obligations are satisfied; if revenue is invoiced through or to a non-resident related party, implement arm's length pricing and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Any allocation to a foreign permanent establishment must be substantiated with time sheets, vessel logs, and contract risk analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs directly attributable to marine heavy driving, including equipment hire, steel procurement, subcontractor fees, charters, and consumables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border equipment leases or subcontracted installation services purchased from related parties, ensure the charge is arm's length; rental or service fees paid to non-residents may trigger Chinese withholding tax (10% statutory, treaty-reduced where applicable) if the income is sourced in China or attributable to a local PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax and surcharges such as urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, property tax, stamp duty, and land use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax on outbound payments (dividends, interest, royalties) is not deductible in the corporate income tax return. Ensure that any tax charged by foreign jurisdictions is booked as foreign tax credit only when a claim is available, and not as deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, including bid and tender costs, marketing fees, and commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a commission or service fee is paid to a non-resident intermediary for services performed wholly outside China, no China WHT is generally due absent a PE; however, the services must be validated by contract and supporting performance evidence. Avoid profit-based commissions, which are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses, including head-office allocations, management fees, legal and professional fees, and office overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees or head-office cost allocations from the overseas parent must meet the arm's length standard and be supported by a cost-sharing arrangement or service agreement; profit-based (i.e., percentage-of-profit) management fees are unequivocally non-deductible under Chinese law. Ensure no double counting with transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, primarily interest on intercompany debt, discount charges, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany interest must be tested against the thin capitalization rule: for a non-financial enterprise, the debt-to-equity ratio cannot exceed 2:1; otherwise, the excess interest is non-deductible. Interest payable to a non-resident creditor is subject to a 10% statutory withholding tax unless a treaty reduces the rate, and the WFOE must withhold and report it. The loan documentation and beneficial ownership of the lender must be preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit (net income) before tax adjustments, after all revenue and expense entries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line must include all global income of the WFOE; if the WFOE has foreign branches or PEs, consolidate their results and separately recognize foreign tax credits. Ensure that revenue from Chinese offshore works is not artificially siphoned to tax-haven entities via invoice skimming or back-to-back arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after statutory tax adjustments, including add-backs of non-deductible amounts, reductions for tax-exempt income, R&D super-deductions, and offset of carryforward losses (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Perform a robust transfer pricing adjustment review before filing: any involuntary adjustment by the tax authority will increase taxable income and attract penalties. Carryforward losses are allowed for 5 years; for High and New Technology Enterprises the period is 10 years. Verify that losses arose from arm's length operations and not from transfer pricing manipulation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of enterprise income tax at 25%, reduced by tax credits (foreign tax credit, equipment credits) and preferential rate reductions (e.g., 15% HNTE rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the tentative tax liability; if subject to DTA relief on foreign-source income, claim foreign tax credit using Form A108000. Simultaneously prepare a reconciliation between booked tax and assessed tax; any discrepancy should be explained in the form to avoid an audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual tax liability after prepaid quarterly tax installments, showing the balance payable or refundable for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance due must be paid by 31 May. For the WFOE, dividend distributions to a non-resident shareholder are not deductible and are not included here; they trigger a separate withholding obligation on dividends at 10% (or treaty rate) that must be filed and paid within the statutory withholding tax deadlines.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual corporate income tax return triggers a monetary penalty of up to RMB 2,000 (or RMB 10,000 for serious cases) under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL), plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax for each day after the statutory deadline. If the late filing is combined with underpayment due to false declaration, Article 63 of TCAL imposes a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax, and criminal liability arises under Criminal Law Article 201 if the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the taxable income, leading to imprisonment of up to 3 years (or 3-7 years for larger amounts) and additional fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law, a non-resident enterprise receiving dividends from a WFOE is subject to a 10% withholding tax unless a bilateral Double Tax Agreement (DTA) reduces the rate. To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) be the beneficial owner of the dividends; (ii) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, evidencing residency in that state; (iii) complete the self-assessment declaration for treaty benefits (as introduced by SAT Announcement No. 35 of 2019), which adopts a 'self-judgment, self-declaration, retention-of-records-for-inspection' mechanism; (iv) submit to the WFOE (as withholding agent) the TRC and a beneficial ownership statement, together with supporting documents (board resolutions, organizational chart, substance evidence such as premises and employees); (v) the WFOE then applies the treaty rate at source when paying the dividend and reports the withholding accordingly. All documents must be retained for at least 10 years for potential tax authority audit; if the beneficial ownership or substance is insufficient (e.g., a conduit entity), the treaty relief is denied and the statutory 10% WHT plus late interest and penalties will apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border interest is 10%; on royalties it is also 10%. Under many DTAs, the rate may be reduced: interest is commonly reduced to 7% (e.g., China-Singapore) or remains 10% (e.g., China-US); royalties generally to 5% or 10% depending on the type of copyright, patent, or know-how, and the treaty partner. The same treaty relief protocol as for dividends applies: the recipient must prove beneficial ownership, provide a TRC, and the WFOE must withhold at the reduced rate only after obtaining the required documentation. Interest and royalties paid to non-residents are subject to the same 10% statutory rate; treaty reductions must be claimed on each payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File transfer pricing documentation is required if, in the preceding fiscal year, the WFOE exceeds any of the following thresholds with related parties: tangible property transfers exceed RMB 200 million; financial asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million; intangible property transfers exceed RMB 100 million; or other related-party transactions exceed RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is required if the total annual related-party transaction value exceeds RMB 1 billion, or if the MNE group's consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion (triggering Country-by-Country Reporting obligations) and the enterprise is designated to prepare a Master File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China enforces the substance-over-form doctrine and a General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law. For an offshore wind piling WFOE, economic substance is demonstrated through actual employees, operational equipment, project management, and risk-taking in China. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for marine installation and piling services are located where the personnel, vessels, and equipment operate; therefore, the income from such services must be reported in China. Merely booking revenue through a Hong Kong or tax-haven related entity without real activity will result in a re-allocation of profit under the arm's-length standard, denial of treaty benefits, and application of anti-abuse penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately omits a substantial portion of revenue derived from offshore wind monopile installation by diverting payments to an offshore shell entity disguised as intercompany loans or non-taxable deposits, or by inflating subcontractor costs through fictitious invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL), the tax authority will recover the evaded tax and impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the amount underpaid. If the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable, Criminal Law Article 201 applies: imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine; for substantial amounts (typically over RMB 100,000 and exceeding 30% of payable tax), imprisonment from 3 to 7 years and heavier fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered, authorized, or knowingly benefitted from the false reporting may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties under Company Law Article 20 through piercing the corporate veil. They may also face exit restriction (travel ban) and blacklisting under TCAL Article 17, civil asset restitution, and criminal imprisonment up to 7 years, plus confiscation of personal assets obtained through the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE engages in related-party transactions exceeding statutory thresholds (e.g., intercompany marine equipment leases, subcontracted installation services, or management fees) but fails to prepare or provide the required Local File or Master File, or the transactional pricing is not at arm's length, resulting in artificially low taxable profit in China and profit shifting to a related entity abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 44 of TCAL and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures (SAT Announcement No. 6 of 2016), the tax authority may re-determine taxable income using a deemed pricing method (typically TNMM) and assess additional tax. The underpaid tax is subject to a fine of 50% to 500% under TCAL Article 64, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05%; failure to provide contemporaneous documentation may trigger an additional 5% monthly interest surcharge on the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the non-arm's-length transactions and failed to ensure documentation compliance can be held personally liable for the resultant tax shortfall if the company's separate legal personality is abused (i.e., personal asset tracing), while exit restrictions and travel bans may be issued for the legal representative. In aggravated cases, criminal tax evasion liability may attach with imprisonment up to 3 years or longer if the underpayment is large.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA Abuse / Phantom Beneficial Ownership (Shell Company)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays dividends or royalties to a non-resident parent or affiliate located in a treaty jurisdiction (e.g., a Hong Kong or Singapore mailbox company) that lacks real economic substance, solely to obtain a reduced treaty withholding tax rate (e.g., 5% on dividends instead of 10%), and files a false beneficial ownership declaration to support the treaty claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT Announcement No. 35 of 2019, the tax authority may deny treaty benefits, re-characterize the payment as Chinese-source income subject to the statutory 10% withholding tax, and impose late interest and penalties. If the false declaration is deemed tax evasion, TCAL Article 63 imposes a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, and Criminal Law Article 201 may prosecute the conduct as tax fraud, leading to imprisonment of 3 to 7 years for significant amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who executed or certified false beneficial ownership declarations face personal civil liability for the additional withholding tax and penalties via the corporate veil doctrine, a travel ban and blacklisting under TCAL Article 17, and criminal liability under the tax fraud provisions. They may also be personally liable to creditors if the corporate façade is pierced, with asset restitution orders and imprisonment up to 7 years in egregious cases.
